examples.en: The gas pipe is old, so it needs to be replaced with a new one.

examples.ko: 공사 중에 가스관을 건드려서 큰일 날 뻔했어요.
examples.en: We touched the gas pipe during construction and nearly had a disaster.
If there is a smell from the gas pipe, report it right away.

examples.ko: 우리 집 가스관은 벽 안쪽으로 지나가요.
examples.en: The gas pipe in our house runs inside the wall.

examples.ko: 가스관 점검 때문에 오늘 오전에 가스가 끊겨요.
examples.en: The gas will be cut off this morning because of the gas pipe inspection.

examples.ko: 가스관과 수도관 중 어느 쪽이 문제인지 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Check whether the gas pipe or the water pipe is the problem.

explain: '관'은 파이프라는 뜻으로, '수도관', '하수관'처럼 다른 말 뒤에 붙어서 쓰여요. 집이나 건물에서 가스가 지나가는 관을 말하고, 공사나 점검 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 가스가 새면 '가스 누출'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The gas pipe is leaking, so there's a smell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 상황을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used for dangerous situations.

phrases.en: There is a gas pipe inspection tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전 검사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for safety inspections.

phrases.example: 우리 동네에서 가스관 공사를 하고 있어요.
phrases.en: They are doing gas pipe work in our neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사 소식이나 안내에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in construction news and notices.

explain_en: '관' means pipe and attaches to other words, as in '수도관' (water pipe) and '하수관' (sewer pipe). It is the pipe that carries gas in a home or building and often appears in talk about construction or inspections. When gas leaks, it is called '가스 누출'.

examples.en: After cleaning the chimney, my face got covered in soot.

examples.ko: 고기 구운 불판의 검댕을 겨우 닦아 냈어요.
examples.en: I barely managed to wipe the soot off the grill plate.
The kids came back covered in soot from playing.

examples.ko: 옷에 검댕만 묻은 게 아니라 냄새도 배었어요.
examples.en: Not only did soot get on my clothes, the smell soaked in too.

examples.ko: 손에 묻은 검댕은 비누로 두 번 씻어야 지워져요.
examples.en: You have to wash the soot on your hands twice with soap to get it off.
Wear gloves so you don't touch the soot.

explain: 비슷한 말로 '그을음'이 있는데, '검댕'은 손이나 얼굴, 냄비에 묻은 검은 가루를 말할 때 자주 써요. '검댕투성이'처럼 '-투성이'를 붙이면 온통 묻은 모습을 나타내요.

phrases.example: 촛불을 켜 두었더니 벽에 그을음이 생겼어요.
phrases.en: After leaving the candle lit, soot formed on the wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷한 말이에요. '그을음'은 불에서 나는 연기가 만든 검은 가루를 널리 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a similar word. 그을음 broadly means black powder made by smoke from a fire.

phrases.en: After cleaning, my hands were covered in soot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-투성이'를 붙여 온통 묻은 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -투성이 describes being covered all over.

phrases.en: Soot got on the bottom of the pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇에 묻었는지 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most basic phrase for saying where soot got stuck.

explain_en: A similar word is '그을음', but '검댕' is often used for black soot stuck on hands, faces or pots. Adding '-투성이' as in '검댕투성이' means being covered all over with it.

examples.ko: 아버지가 경운기에 고추를 가득 싣고 오셨어요.
examples.en: My father came back with the cultivator full of chili peppers.
I was late because I was stuck behind a cultivator on a country road.

examples.ko: 경운기 소리가 들리면 아침이 시작된 느낌이에요.
examples.en: When I hear the cultivator's sound, it feels like the morning has begun.
In the farming season, neighbors borrow and use each other's cultivators.

examples.ko: 경운기가 고장 나서 밭을 갈지 못했어요.
examples.en: The cultivator broke down, so we couldn't plow the field.

examples.ko: 마을 어귀에 낡은 경운기 한 대가 서 있어요.
examples.en: An old cultivator is parked at the entrance of the village.

explain: 밭을 갈거나 짐을 나르는 농사용 기계라서 시골 이야기에서 자주 나와요. '경운기를 몰다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Grandfather drove the cultivator out to the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경운기를 운전한다는 뜻으로, 시골 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to drive a cultivator; the most common collocation in country-life stories.

phrases.en: Every spring my father plows the field with a cultivator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경운기의 가장 큰 쓰임인 밭 갈기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the main use of a cultivator: plowing a field.
phrases.en_equiv: to plow a field with a cultivator

phrases.en: I wake up every morning to the sound of a cultivator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시골 마을의 풍경을 소리로 나타낼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to evoke the sounds of a country village.

explain_en: It is a farm machine used for plowing fields and carrying loads, so it often comes up in stories about the countryside. People say '경운기를 몰다' for driving one.

examples.en: High-voltage lines run a long way over the mountain.
It is dangerous to fly a kite near high-voltage lines.

examples.ko: 고압선 철탑이 집 근처에 생겨서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: A high-voltage pylon was built near my house, and I am worried.

examples.ko: 고압선 아래에는 건물을 지을 수 없어요.
examples.en: You cannot build under high-voltage lines.
A high-voltage line broke because of the typhoon.
The road is blocked because of high-voltage line work.

explain: 집 앞 전봇대에 걸린 일반 선은 그냥 '전선'이라고 하고, '고압선'은 전압이 높은 굵은 선이나 철탑의 선을 말할 때 써요. '고압선 조심' 같은 경고 문구에도 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 산 위에 고압선 철탑이 길게 서 있어요.
phrases.en: High-voltage towers stand in a long line on the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고압선을 걸어 두는 큰 탑을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the big towers that carry the cables.

phrases.en: This road has a 'Beware of high-voltage lines' sign.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경고 문구로 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen as a warning sign.

phrases.en: It's hard to build a house under high-voltage lines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위치를 말할 때 '아래'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 아래 to describe the location.

explain_en: The ordinary wires on a utility pole are just called '전선', while '고압선' refers to the thick high-voltage lines, such as those on pylons. It also appears in warnings like '고압선 조심'.

examples.ko: 촛불을 켜 두었더니 유리에 그을음이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I left a candle burning, and soot formed on the glass.

examples.ko: 오래된 난로에서 그을음이 나와 손에 묻었어요.
examples.en: Soot came out of the old stove and got on my hands.
A lot of soot has built up in the chimney.
Black soot has stuck to the bottom of the pot.
Smoke rose and soot formed on the ceiling.
I wiped the soot off my face with my hand.

explain: 불이 탈 때 생기는 검은 가루예요. '검댕'이라고도 하고, '그을리다'와 짝으로 외우면 쉬워요. 발음은 [그으름]이에요.

phrases.en: I wiped the soot off the wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청소할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing when talking about cleaning.

phrases.en: Soot built up on the old chimney.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랫동안 쌓여서 덮인 모습을 말할 때 '끼다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '끼다' describes soot building up and covering a surface over time.

phrases.en: Soot got on my hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그을음'과 비슷한 말인데, 손이나 얼굴에 묻은 검은 가루를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '그을음', often used for black residue on hands or face.

explain_en: It is the black powder produced when something burns. It is also called '검댕', and it is easy to learn together with '그을리다'. It is pronounced [그으름].

examples.ko: 아이들이 있는 집에서는 남아나는 물건이 없어요.
examples.en: In a house with kids, nothing survives intact.

examples.ko: 이렇게 험하게 쓰면 신발이 남아나지 않아요.
examples.en: If you wear shoes this roughly, they won't last.
My salary doesn't stay with me, and I'm worried.

examples.ko: 친구들이 다 먹어서 남아나는 과자가 없어요.
examples.en: My friends ate everything, so no snacks are left.

examples.ko: 이사하는 동안 남아난 그릇이 하나도 없었어요.
examples.en: Not a single dish survived the move.
Because of the cat, no curtain survives.

explain: 거의 부정문에서 '~이/가 남아나지 않는다', '남아나는 게 없다'로 써요. 물건이 계속 망가지거나 돈이 금방 없어질 때 투덜대는 느낌으로 말해요.

phrases.example: 아이들이 있는 집에서는 컵이 남아나지 않아요.
phrases.en: In a house with kids, no cup survives.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 다 망가질 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common negative form for things getting broken one after another.

phrases.example: 우리 강아지 때문에 남아나는 게 없어요.
phrases.en: Because of our puppy, nothing is left intact.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 투덜대는 말투로 '다 망가진다'고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said in a grumbling tone, meaning everything gets ruined.

phrases.example: 그렇게 험하게 쓰면 남아날 수가 없어요.
phrases.en: If you use it that roughly, it can't last.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그럴 수밖에 없다는 뜻을 담아 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses that it can't help but be ruined.

explain_en: It is used almost only in negative forms like '~이/가 남아나지 않는다' or '남아나는 게 없다'. It carries a grumbling tone when things keep breaking or money vanishes quickly.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에는 낡은 전선이 누전되기 쉬워요.
examples.en: On rainy days, old wires easily leak current.
Current leaked and the breaker in my house tripped.

examples.ko: 누전된 곳이 없는지 전기 기사님이 점검해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The electrician checked whether there were any places leaking current.

examples.ko: 습기가 많은 화장실은 누전될 수 있으니 조심하세요.
examples.en: A humid bathroom can leak current, so be careful.

examples.ko: 집 안 어디선가 누전되는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems like current is leaking somewhere in the house.
I called a company to check whether there was a current leak.

explain: '누전이 돼요'처럼 명사로도 쓰고, 보통 '차단기가 내려가다'와 함께 나와요. 비슷해 보이는 '합선'은 전선끼리 닿아서 불꽃이 나는 거라 달라요.

phrases.example: 낡은 콘센트가 누전이 돼서 불이 날 뻔했어요.
phrases.en: The old outlet leaked electricity and almost caused a fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '누전'에 '이 되다'를 붙여 '누전되다' 대신 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun '누전' with '이 되다', an alternative to '누전되다'.

phrases.en: Electrical leakage accidents happen often in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 보는 말로, 전기가 새서 난 사고를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in the news, meaning accidents caused by leaking electricity.

phrases.en: The circuit breaker tripped and the power went out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전기가 새면 자동으로 전기를 끊는 장치예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A device that cuts the power automatically when electricity leaks.

explain_en: You can also use the noun form, as in '누전이 돼요', and it usually appears together with '차단기가 내려가다' (the breaker trips). The similar-looking '합선' is different: it is when wires touch and spark.

examples.en: The road got covered in mud because of the rain.

examples.ko: 여러 소리가 뒤범벅돼서 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: Many sounds are mixed together, so I can't hear well.
Put the papers in a file so they don't get mixed up.
My feelings were all jumbled together and I couldn't speak.
My clothes ended up smeared all over with paint.

examples.ko: 기억이 뒤범벅되어 정확히 생각이 안 나요.
examples.en: My memories are muddled, so I can't recall exactly.

explain: '뒤범벅이 되다'와 같은 말인데 더 짧게 붙여서 써요. 지저분하게 묻거나 여러 가지가 섞인 상태 모두에 쓰고, 마음이나 기억처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I washed the clothes drenched in sweat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며 줘요. 어떤 것으로 뒤범벅됐는지는 '~으로'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies the noun after it. Use ~으로 to say what it is covered or mixed with.

phrases.en: My memories are all jumbled and I can't tell the order.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒤범벅되다'와 같은 뜻이지만 조금 더 풀어서 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 뒤범벅되다, just in a slightly longer form.

phrases.example: 두 재료가 뒤범벅되지 않게 따로 담으세요.
phrases.en: Put the two ingredients in separate containers so they don't get mixed up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 섞이는 것을 막고 싶을 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form for saying you want to keep things from getting mixed together.
phrases.en_equiv: so that they don't get mixed up

explain_en: It means the same as '뒤범벅이 되다' in a shorter, joined form. It covers both being smeared messily and having many things mixed up, and can also be used for unseen things like feelings or memories.

examples.ko: 할아버지 묘비에 가족 이름이 새겨져 있어요.
examples.en: The family's names are carved on my grandfather's tombstone.
I laid flowers in front of the tombstone.

examples.ko: 오래된 묘비의 글씨가 닳아서 읽기 어려워요.
examples.en: The writing on the old tombstone is worn away and hard to read.

examples.ko: 묘비가 비바람에 낡아서 새로 만들기로 했어요.
examples.en: The tombstone was weathered by wind and rain, so we decided to make a new one.

examples.ko: 여행 중에 유명한 시인의 묘비를 보러 갔어요.
examples.en: On my trip, I went to see a famous poet's tombstone.
Only the tombstone was left standing alone.

explain: 무덤 앞에 세운 비석을 말해요. '비석'은 기념하려고 세운 돌에도 두루 쓰지만 '묘비'는 무덤에만 써요. 묘비에 새긴 글은 '묘비명'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The family put up a tombstone for my father.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무덤 앞에 비석을 만들어 세운다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means setting up a stone in front of a grave.

phrases.en: We carved a short poem as the epitaph.
phrases.nuance_ko: 묘비에 새긴 글을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for the writing carved on a tombstone.

phrases.example: 묘비 앞에서 한참 동안 인사를 드렸어요.
phrases.en: I paid my respects in front of the tombstone for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성묘할 때 장소를 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A usage for naming the spot when visiting a grave.

explain_en: It means a stone marker set up at a grave. '비석' is used broadly for stones set up as monuments, but '묘비' is only for graves. The words carved on it are called '묘비명' (epitaph).

examples.en: I almost tripped on the threshold.
The child is standing on the threshold.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 문지방을 밟으면 복이 나간다고 했어요.
examples.en: In the old days, people said that stepping on the threshold makes good luck leave.
The threshold is high, so it's hard for a wheelchair to get in.

examples.ko: 문지방 위에 앉지 말고 안으로 들어오세요.
examples.en: Don't sit on the threshold; come inside.
My foot caught on the threshold and I hurt my toe.

explain: '문턱'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '문턱'이 더 흔해요. '문지방을 밟지 마라'처럼 어른들이 하는 옛말에 자주 나와요. 비유로 쓰는 '문턱이 높다'(들어가기 어렵다)는 '문턱'과 같이 외워 두세요.

phrases.example: 그는 그 가게를 문지방이 닳도록 드나들었어요.
phrases.en: He went in and out of that shop all the time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곳을 아주 자주 드나든다는 뜻의 과장 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An exaggeration meaning someone visits a place extremely often.
phrases.en_equiv: wear a path to the door

explain_en: It means almost the same as '문턱', and '문턱' is more common in daily talk. It often appears in old sayings from elders like 'don't step on the threshold'. The figurative '문턱이 높다' (hard to get into) is best learned with '문턱'.

examples.en: After moving in, I put a nameplate on the front gate.
The name is written in big letters on the nameplate.
The old nameplate was worn out, so we replaced it.

examples.ko: 집을 찾을 때 문패 번호를 확인하세요.
examples.en: When you look for the house, check the number on the nameplate.

examples.ko: 문패는 대문 옆 벽에 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The nameplate is attached to the wall next to the gate.

examples.ko: 요즘 아파트에는 문패가 없는 집이 많아요.
examples.en: These days, many apartment homes have no nameplate.

explain: 집 대문이나 현관 옆에 달아 두는 이름이나 주소 표시예요. 요즘 아파트는 호수만 쓰는 경우가 많아서 문패는 주로 단독주택에서 볼 수 있어요. 가게나 사무실의 이름표는 보통 '간판'이나 '명패'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I hung a nameplate on the gate of my new house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '달다'와 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used much like 달다 (to put up).

phrases.en: I found my friend's house by looking at the nameplate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문패로 집을 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you check a house by its nameplate.

phrases.en: The nameplate on the gate is very worn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래되어 헐었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the plate has become old and worn.

explain_en: It is the name or address sign hung by the gate or front door of a house. Apartments often show only a unit number, so nameplates are mostly seen on detached houses. For shops and offices, people usually say '간판' (signboard) or '명패' (desk or door name plate) instead.

examples.ko: 골목에 방범등이 생겨서 밤길이 덜 무서워요.
examples.en: A security light was installed in the alley, so the night road is less scary.

examples.ko: 주민센터에 방범등을 더 달아 달라고 요청했어요.
examples.en: I asked the community center to put up more security lights.
The security light turns on by itself when the sun goes down.

examples.ko: 방범등 덕분에 늦게 퇴근해도 안심이 돼요.
examples.en: Thanks to the security light, I feel safe even when I leave work late.
The security light went out, so I should call the district office.

examples.ko: 우리 아파트 주차장에도 방범등을 새로 설치했어요.
examples.en: They also installed a new security light in our apartment parking lot.

explain: '가로등'은 큰길을 밝히는 등이고, 방범등은 골목이나 주택가의 안전을 위해 다는 등이라서 동네 소식이나 민원 이야기에 자주 나와요. '달다, 설치하다, 켜지다, 고장 나다' 같은 말과 함께 써요.

phrases.en: We installed a security light at the entrance of the alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 등을 설치할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic verb phrase for putting up a light.

phrases.en: When the sun sets, the security light turns on by itself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 켜지는 것을 말할 때 '켜지다'를 써요. 사람이 켜면 '켜다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 켜지다 describes it coming on by itself; if someone switches it on, use 켜다.

phrases.en: The security light is broken, so the alley is dark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동네 민원을 이야기할 때 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard when talking about neighborhood complaints.

explain_en: '가로등' (street lamp) lights up main roads, while 방범등 is the light put in alleys and residential areas for safety, so it often comes up in neighborhood news and complaints. It goes with verbs like '달다', '설치하다', '켜지다' and '고장 나다'.

examples.ko: 샤워기 배수구가 막혀서 물이 안 내려가요.
examples.en: The shower drain is clogged, so the water won't go down.
There is a lot of hair stuck in the drain.
A smell came up from the drain, so I cleaned it.
I bought a product to unclog the sink drain.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 길가 배수구로 물이 넘쳤어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so water overflowed from the drain by the road.

examples.ko: 배수구 덮개는 자주 씻어 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You need to wash the drain cover often.

explain: 욕실이나 싱크대, 길가에서 물이 빠져나가는 구멍이에요. '하수구'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 하수구는 더러운 물이 흘러가는 길이나 관까지 넓게 가리켜요.

phrases.en: The sink drain is clogged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 안 내려갈 때 가장 먼저 떠오르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The first phrase that comes to mind when water won't go down.

phrases.en: I unclogged the blocked drain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막힌 곳을 시원하게 통하게 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you clear a blockage so water flows again.

phrases.en: I clean the bathroom drain every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리카락이나 때를 치우는 일상적인 청소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to everyday cleaning of hair and dirt from the drain.

explain_en: It is the opening where water drains away in a bathroom, sink or roadside. '하수구' is used similarly, but it can also refer more broadly to the channel or pipe that carries dirty water.

examples.en: New security lights were installed in every alley.
Thanks to the security lights, walking at night is less scary.

examples.ko: 주민들이 보안등을 더 달아 달라고 요청했어요.
examples.en: Residents asked for more security lights to be put up.
Children are playing under the glow of the security light.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 보안등은 해가 지면 저절로 켜져요.
examples.en: The security lights in our neighborhood turn on by themselves at sunset.

examples.ko: 고장 난 보안등에 안내문이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: A notice is stuck on the broken security light.

explain: 골목이나 주택가의 밤길을 안전하게 하려고 세운 등이에요. 큰길의 '가로등'과 비슷하지만 방범 목적이 더 강해요. 동네 민원이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: When the sun set, the security lights came on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어두워질 때 등이 저절로 켜지는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes lights coming on as it gets dark.

phrases.example: 어두운 골목에 보안등을 달아 달라고 신청했어요.
phrases.en: I applied to have a security light installed in the dark alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 등을 설치한다는 뜻으로, 동네 일을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means installing a light; common in talk about neighborhood matters.

phrases.en: The streetlights are shining brightly on the main road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보안등'과 비슷하지만 '가로등'은 길을 비추는 큰길의 등을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 보안등, but 가로등 means the lights along main roads.

explain_en: These are lights set up in alleys and residential areas to make night streets safer. They are similar to '가로등' (street lamps) on main roads but have a stronger crime-prevention purpose. They come up in neighborhood complaints and news.

examples.ko: 밤에 쥐가 부스럭거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: A mouse was rustling at night, so I couldn't sleep.
The person next to me keeps rustling a plastic bag.

examples.ko: 영화 중에 과자를 부스럭거리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't rustle snack bags during a movie.
I hear someone rustling around in the room.
The child rustled around under the blanket and then got up.
When I walk on fallen leaves, they rustle under my feet.

explain: 마른 종이, 비닐, 낙엽처럼 마른 것이 스치는 소리가 나거나 그런 소리를 내며 움직인다는 말이에요. '부스럭대다'도 같은 뜻이에요. '바스락거리다'는 조금 더 가볍고 작은 소리 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling rustled around at dawn and woke me up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부스럭거리다'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때 조금 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 부스럭거리다, a bit more casual.

phrases.en: I hear a rustling sound in the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 설명할 때 '-는'을 붙여서 명사 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the -는 form before 소리 to describe the sound.

phrases.en: Fallen leaves rustle when you step on them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부스럭거리다'보다 가볍고 작은 소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter, smaller sound than 부스럭거리다.

explain_en: It describes the dry sound of things like paper, plastic or leaves rubbing together, or moving while making that sound. '부스럭대다' means the same thing. '바스락거리다' feels a little lighter and softer in sound.

examples.en: They piled rice high on my plate.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 온 집의 창가에 먼지가 수북이 쌓였어요.
examples.en: Dust had piled up on the windowsill since I hadn't been home in a while.
Fallen leaves lay piled in heaps across the yard.

examples.ko: 배가 고파서 밥을 수북이 퍼서 먹었어요.
examples.en: I was hungry, so I scooped a heaping portion of rice and ate it.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 서류가 수북이 쌓인 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw documents piled high on the desk.

examples.ko: 눈이 수북이 쌓여서 차가 못 다녀요.
examples.en: Snow has piled up deep, so cars can't get through.

explain: '수북하다'의 부사형이에요. '가득'은 그릇이 꽉 찬 것이고, '수북이'는 그릇 위로 솟아오를 만큼 쌓인 모양이에요.

phrases.en: The plate is heaped with rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '수북이'의 기본이 되는 형용사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective that 수북이 comes from.

phrases.en: I heaped fruit in the bowl.
phrases.nuance_ko: '담다'와 함께 쓰면 그릇 위로 솟게 가득 담는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 담다, it means filling above the rim.

phrases.en: The snow piled up deep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 되풀이해서 쌓인 모습을 더 생생하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The repeated form makes the piling more vivid.

explain_en: It is the adverb form of '수북하다'. '가득' means filled to the brim, while '수북이' means piled up so high it rises above the rim.

examples.en: I put rice and seasoned vegetables in a big bowl and mixed them.

examples.ko: 엄마가 양푼에 떡볶이를 가득 담아 주셨어요.
examples.en: Mom filled a big bowl with tteokbokki for us.

examples.ko: 양푼 비빔밥은 숟가락으로 막 비벼 먹어야 맛있어요.
examples.en: Bibimbap in a big bowl tastes best when you mix it roughly with a spoon.
Where did our big bowl go?

examples.ko: 양푼 하나에 다섯 명이 같이 먹었어요.
examples.en: Five of us ate together from one big bowl.
You can use a big bowl for a long time even if it gets dented.

explain: 음식을 담거나 비빌 때 쓰는 큰 그릇이에요. '양푼 비빔밥'처럼 여럿이 함께 먹는 편한 분위기와 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I shared a big bowl of bibimbap with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 그릇에 비벼서 여럿이 같이 먹는 편한 분위기의 음식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual dish mixed in a big bowl and shared with many people.

phrases.en: I filled the big bowl with kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 그릇에 음식을 많이 담는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means putting a lot of food into a large bowl.
phrases.en_equiv: to put in a big bowl

phrases.en: I brought a big bowl full of fruit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그릇이 크고 음식이 넉넉하다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of a large bowl with plenty of food.

explain_en: It is a big bowl used for holding or mixing food. It fits the relaxed mood of eating together, as in '양푼 비빔밥'.

examples.ko: 그는 밧줄 한쪽 끝을 묶어 올가미를 만들었어요.
examples.en: He tied one end of the rope and made a loop snare.
Be careful not to get your foot caught in the snare.
The rabbit was caught in a snare and couldn't move.

examples.ko: 그 계약은 사실 사기꾼이 파 놓은 올가미였어요.
examples.en: That contract was actually a trap set by a swindler.
I want to get away from rules that feel like a trap.

examples.ko: 올가미를 던져 말을 잡는 영상을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a video of someone throwing a lasso to catch a horse.

explain: 줄 끝을 고리로 만들어 동물이나 물건을 잡는 도구예요. 비유로 '빠져나오기 힘든 함정'이라는 뜻으로도 써요. '덫'은 여러 가지 장치를 모두 가리켜서 조금 더 넓어요.

phrases.en: A rabbit got caught in the snare.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이나 사람이 걸려 잡힌 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes being caught in a snare.
phrases.en_equiv: to get caught in a snare

phrases.en: The cowboy threw a lasso toward the horse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄 고리를 던져 잡는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes throwing a loop of rope to catch something.

phrases.en: The hunter set a trap in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '올가미'보다 넓게 여러 가지 장치를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 올가미, covering all kinds of traps.

explain_en: It is a tool made by forming a loop at the end of a rope to catch an animal or object. Figuratively it also means a trap that is hard to escape. '덫' is a little broader, covering all kinds of trapping devices.

examples.en: The plate fell and smashed with a crash.
The window shattered with a loud crash.
The shelf collapsed with a crash and I was startled.
A cat passing by knocked a cup down with a crash.
I heard a crash and ran to the kitchen.

examples.ko: 화분이 와장창 넘어지는 소리에 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up at the sound of a flowerpot crashing over.

explain: 물건이 한꺼번에 깨지거나 무너질 때 나는 요란한 소리예요. '쨍그랑'은 유리나 그릇이 깨지는 소리에 주로 쓰고, '와장창'은 더 크고 여러 개가 무너지는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The glass bottle shattered with a crash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 '깨지다'를 함께 쓴 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 깨지다.

phrases.en: The stacked boxes collapsed with a crash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 개가 한꺼번에 무너지는 큰 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the loud sound of many things collapsing at once.

phrases.example: 컵이 바닥에 떨어져서 쨍그랑 소리가 났어요.
phrases.en: The cup fell on the floor and made a clanging crash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 소리말로, 유리나 그릇 하나가 깨지는 소리에 주로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar sound word, mainly for a single glass or dish breaking.

explain_en: It is the loud sound of things breaking or collapsing all at once. '쨍그랑' is mainly the sound of glass or dishes breaking, while '와장창' feels bigger and more like many things falling apart.

examples.en: They repainted the exterior wall of the building.
The outer wall is cracked, so rain leaks in.

examples.ko: 아파트 외벽 공사 때문에 소리가 커요.
examples.en: It's loud because of the exterior wall work at the apartment.
Ivy is growing on the outside wall.
In winter, a house with thick outer walls is warm.
Workers hang from ropes to clean the exterior wall.

explain: 건물의 바깥쪽을 둘러싼 벽이에요. 반대말은 안쪽의 '내벽'이에요. 공사나 건축 이야기에 자주 나오고, 평소에는 그냥 '벽'이라고 해도 돼요.

phrases.en: Next year they will do exterior wall work on the apartment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물 겉벽을 고치거나 칠하는 일을 말해요. 건축 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Work to repair or paint a building's outer wall, common in construction talk.

phrases.en: We painted the outer wall white.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이나 페인트를 바꿀 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for changing the color or paint of a building.

phrases.en: The outer wall cracked because of the earthquake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벽이 갈라진 상태를 말할 때 써요. '갈라지다'보다 얇은 틈 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a cracked wall, with a feel of a thin crack rather than a big split.

explain_en: It is the wall on the outside of a building, and its opposite is 내벽, the inner wall. It appears in construction talk, though in casual speech people often just say 벽.

examples.ko: 책상 서랍이 잡동사니로 가득 차 있어요.
examples.en: The desk drawer is full of odds and ends.

examples.ko: 창고에서 잡동사니를 정리하다가 옛 사진을 찾았어요.
examples.en: While sorting junk in the storeroom, I found old photos.
Before moving, I'd better throw away the clutter first.
This box has nothing but odds and ends in it.
There is so much clutter that the room looks small.

examples.ko: 가방 속 잡동사니 때문에 열쇠를 못 찾겠어요.
examples.en: I can't find my keys because of all the stuff in my bag.

explain: 쓸모가 있는지 없는지 애매한 자잘한 물건들이 뒤섞여 있는 것을 말해요. 완전한 쓰레기와 달리 아직 버리지 않고 모아 둔 물건이라는 느낌이 있어요. '잡동사니를 정리하다/버리다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Odds and ends are piled up on the balcony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자잘한 물건이 치우지 않은 채 많아졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means small items have piled up without being tidied.

phrases.en: I cleared out all the clutter before moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정리하다'보다 눈앞에서 없앤다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels more like removing things from sight than '정리하다'.

phrases.en: I found batteries in the junk box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 가지 작은 물건을 아무렇게나 넣어 둔 상자를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a box where various small items are tossed in.

explain_en: It refers to small items of unclear use that are jumbled together. Unlike pure trash, it has a feel of things you have kept and not yet thrown away. It is often used as '잡동사니를 정리하다/버리다'.

examples.en: When the athlete lit the torch, applause poured in.
Be careful when you light the burner.

examples.ko: 로켓 엔진을 점화한 지 몇 초 만에 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: The rocket lifted off just seconds after the engine was ignited.
I tried to light the candle with a lighter.
Check safety first, and then light it.
A loud noise came the moment it was ignited.

explain: 성화, 엔진, 버너처럼 불을 붙여 작동시키는 것이 목적어로 와요. 일상에서는 '불을 붙이다'나 '불을 켜다'라고 말하고, '점화하다'는 설명서나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I lit the gas stove.
phrases.nuance_ko: '점화하다'보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural in daily conversation than '점화하다'.

phrases.en: When the engine ignited, the rocket went up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불이 붙어 작동하기 시작한다는 뜻으로, 주어가 불이 붙는 쪽이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form: the thing itself catches fire and starts working.

phrases.en: Put the water on after lighting the burner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ 뒤에'를 붙여 순서를 말하는 연결형이에요. 설명서에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form for giving steps, often seen in instructions.

explain_en: Its objects are things lit to start working, such as torches, engines and burners. In daily life people say '불을 붙이다' or '불을 켜다', and '점화하다' appears more in manuals and news.

examples.en: The whole town lost power because of the storm.
The power suddenly went out and I could not see anything.
If the building loses power, the elevators stop.
While the power was out, we lit candles and talked.
I bought a flashlight in case the power goes out at night.

examples.ko: 어젯밤에 정전되었는데 한 시간 뒤에 들어왔어요.
examples.en: The power went out last night and came back an hour later.

explain: 전기가 갑자기 끊길 때 써요. 일상에서는 '정전이 되다', '불이 나가다'라고 더 많이 말해요. 전기가 다시 들어오면 '전기가 들어오다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: There was a power outage in our neighborhood last night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정전되다'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '정전되다' and common in spoken Korean.

phrases.en: The lights suddenly went out and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual spoken expression.

phrases.en: The electricity came back on an hour later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정전이 끝났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the outage is over.

explain_en: Use it when electricity is suddenly cut. In daily speech people more often say '정전이 되다' or '불이 나가다'. When power returns, you say '전기가 들어오다'.

examples.ko: 비 때문에 창문에 판자를 대 놓았어요.
examples.en: Because of the rain, I boarded up the window.
The man cut a plank and made a bookshelf.

examples.ko: 산비탈에 낡은 판자로 지은 집이 아직 몇 채 남아 있어요.
examples.en: A few houses built of old boards still remain on the hillside.

examples.ko: 판자가 썩어서 이 다리는 건너기 위험해요.
examples.en: The boards are rotten, so this bridge is dangerous to cross.
This board is thick and hard, so it is sturdy.

examples.ko: 마당 한쪽에 남은 판자를 쌓아 두었어요.
examples.en: I stacked the leftover planks in one corner of the yard.

explain: 얇고 넓게 자른 나무가 '판자'이고, 두껍고 긴 나무는 '각목'이라고 해서 모양으로 이름이 갈려요. '판자촌'은 낡은 판자로 지은 집이 모인 동네를 가리키는 말로 옛날 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I put a board over the hole in the wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무언가를 막거나 덮으려고 판자를 붙일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when attaching a board to cover or block something.

phrases.en: Wooden planks are piled up in the storage room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료가 나무라는 것을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make clear that the material is wood.

phrases.en: The children made a small house out of boards.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료가 판자라고 말할 때 '-(으)로'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -(으)로 to say the material is board.

explain_en: A '판자' is a thin, wide cut of wood, while a thick, long piece is called a '각목'. The word '판자촌' (shanty town) comes up often in stories about the past.

examples.en: The drain is clogged, so the water won't go down.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 하수구에서 물이 넘쳐요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, water overflows from the drain.
Hair often gets stuck in the drain.
A sewer smell came up, so I opened the window.
I dropped my key down the drain.
Drains need to be cleaned regularly.

explain: 원래 길 아래 큰 물길은 '하수구', 집 안 욕실이나 싱크대의 구멍은 '배수구'라고 구별해요. 하지만 일상에서는 집 안의 구멍도 '하수구'라고 하는 사람이 많아요.

phrases.en: There's a sewer smell in the bathroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이나 길에서 나는 나쁜 냄새를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for bad smells in the home or street.

phrases.en: I cleaned the sink drain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 안의 물 빠지는 구멍은 '배수구'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The drain hole inside a house is also called 배수구.

phrases.en: You must not pour oil down the drain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경이나 생활 규칙을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in talk about environment or household rules.

explain_en: Strictly, the large channel under the street is 하수구 and the hole in a bathroom or sink is 배수구. In daily life, though, many people call the one at home 하수구 as well.

examples.en: I turned on the kitchen fan and grilled fish.

examples.ko: 화장실 환풍기가 고장 나서 소리가 커요.
examples.en: The bathroom fan is broken, so it makes a lot of noise.
After I left the fan on, the smell went away.
Dust had built up on the fan, so I cleaned it.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 환풍기가 잘 돌아가서 냄새가 안 나요.
examples.en: This restaurant's fans run well, so there is no smell.

examples.ko: 환풍기 소리가 시끄러워서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: The fan is so loud that I can't sleep.

explain: 공기를 바꾸는 일은 '환기'이고, 그 일을 하는 기계가 '환풍기'예요. 부엌의 큰 환풍기는 '후드'라고도 많이 불러요. '환풍기를 켜다/끄다/틀다', '환풍기가 돌아가다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I turn off the exhaust fan when I finish cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '켜다'의 반대 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of turning it on (켜다).

phrases.en: The fan keeps running, so it is noisy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환풍기가 작동하고 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the fan running.

phrases.en: I turned on the range hood and grilled meat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부엌 환풍기를 일상에서 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday word for the kitchen exhaust fan.

explain_en: Swapping the air in a room is '환기', and the machine that does it is a '환풍기'. The large fan above a stove is also commonly called a '후드'. You say '환풍기를 켜다/끄다/틀다' and '환풍기가 돌아가다'.
